newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Pakhoed sees improved oil storage market.
newsitem.headline: Pakhoed sees improved oil storage market.

text.p: Dutch tank storage and shipping company Koninklijke Pakhoed NV said on Tuesday the European oil storage market was improving after a year of hardship.

"The market has noticeably improved from January 1. A contango market emerged in the first two months of this year and we have done reasonably well," executive board member Gerard Krans told a news conference.
He said capacity utilisation had picked up, but the market was not strong enough for rates to have risen.
"We have already seen better occupancy levels, but prices have not risen yet," he said.
Pakhoed itself expects a turnaround in its Rotterdam storage activities which were loss-making last year.
"In the whole year, we expect a return to profit (in European oil storage)," said chairman Klaas Westdijk.

However, while Pakhoed welcomed the healthier oil storage market, it acknowledged the turnaround in its Rotterdam business would be largely the result of the restructuring efforts forced on the company last year.
By the middle of this year, its Rotterdam-based workforce will fall to 300. It will also be among the first companies to dismantle storage capacity in Rotterdam.
Last year, losses in Pakhoed's Rotterdam operations dragged down overall profits in tank storage. In Europe, net profit in tank storage from ordinary operations fell by 30 percent.

"In Rotterdam, a number of factors hit us on the oil side. The refineries were holding lower storage, trading companies didn't want to store and there was less oil from the Middle East coming to Europe," said executive board member Ton Spoor.
"In the past we operated in a seller's market. Now it is clearly a buyer's market," he added.

The comments came after Pakhoed announced a rise in 1996 net profit from ordinary operations of 12 percent to 138.3 million guilders. However, restructuring charges sliced the 1996 total net profit to 75.5 million guilders, well below 1995's 121.5 million guilders.
